text:
maria: Heads-up — I ran a quick perf sweep on small-batch traffic this morning. p95 looks fine but p99 spikes on prefill-heavy requests.
jon: Can you paste the breakdown you saw? Prefill vs decode numbers?
maria: Sure. Sample median request (seq_len=64, model=xl-quant): prefill=18ms, decode=6ms, but p99 prefill jumps to ~240ms on some nodes.
kevin: That smells like kernel fallback or KV miss / cold-path. Did you capture kernel choices?
maria: Yep. On the problematic nodes the runtime switched from fast-gemm to fallback for prefill at ~32 token boundary due to workspace fragmentation. Logs: ```KERNEL_SELECT: fast_gemm @ tokens<=31 -> fallback_sparse @ tokens>31; workspace_alloc_fail=1```
anya: Oof. Is that deterministic by request size distribution or due to memory noise from concurrent jobs?
jon: From earlier traces, tiny microbatches (batch=1, bursty arrivals) increase allocator churn and cause occasional fallback. Two levers: increase microbatch window (add 2-3ms delay) or change allocator to prefer contiguous workspace for prefill.
kevin: Increasing microbatching helps throughput but could violate SLO for latency-sensitive routes. Which routes are we willing to nudge?
maria: Customer A (chat-interactive) must keep p95<50ms — they can’t tolerate added batching delay. Customer B (async summarization) can accept extra 10ms for better tail.
anya: Could we do adaptive microbatching: 0ms when latency budget tight; up to 6ms when we detect prefill-heavy pattern. Similar to token-phase gating we discussed last quarter.
jon: Agree. Also consider kernel prewarming: if we detect pattern of prefill>30 tokens, proactively keep the fast_gemm kernel resident and reserve workspace ahead of time. That would avoid the alloc_fail event.
kevin: Prewarming helps but costs memory. We should quantify unit-econ: extra reserved workspace per device vs p99 ms saved. Any profiling numbers?
maria: Quick numbers from the sweep: prewarming 256KB per device cut those p99 spikes on 3/5 nodes we repro'd, p99 down from 240ms -> 34ms. Memory cost ~0.5% of device VRAM on A100-40GB.
jon: That's promising. For routes that cannot accept batching delay, prewarm + strict allocator for prefill seems best. For throughput-focused routes, adaptive microbatch + larger kernel window wins.
anya: We also saw KV cache misses increasing during these spikes. Might be related: when kernel fallback happens, KV cache warmup deferred leading to extra decode work later. Sequence: alloc_fail -> fallback prefill -> KV not populated -> later decode does extra KV fills -> tail worsens.
kevin: Good catch. So fix order: avoid fallback OR ensure fallback path populates KV the same way. Fallback path currently skips async KV prefetch to save cycles. We should change that.
maria: Proposed short term plan: (1) safe prewarm of fast_gemm workspace on latency-critical routes (config knob), (2) ensure fallback path triggers KV prefill, (3) deploy adaptive microbatch controller for throughput routes, (4) add telemetry counters: kernel_fallback_count, workspace_alloc_fail, kv_miss_after_prefill.
jon: I'll draft a rollout: start with a canary on staging instances for Customer A config, measure p95/p99 and VRAM consumption.
anya: Also add a flamegraph capture around one repro request for both paths so we can show exact time spent in allocator, kernel_select, and KV logic.
kevin: For long term: redesign allocator to use per-stream slab pools to avoid fragmentation during interleaved small-batch traffic. Low risk? medium. Timeline 2-4 sprints.
maria: OK — I'll open a GitHub PR for the fallback KV change and add the telemetry. jon, can you own the canary plan? kevin/anya, add allocator design ticket and prewarm config.
deploy-bot: deploy request posted: PR #3781 -> staging (tags: prewarm, kv-fallback)
jon: ACK. Can we get flamegraph captures in prod for 1% sampled requests? Need opt-in toggle.
maria: Added sampling flag to telemetry task list.
kevin: One more note — kernel selection heuristic threshold currently tuned on seq_len distribution from last year. With longer chat messages now, we might shift threshold from 31->48 tokens to reduce churn. That plus prewarm might eliminate most spikes.
anya: Sounds good. Prioritization: high for fallback KV change + telemetry, medium for prewarm config rollout, low for allocator rewrite (but schedule it).
maria: I'll summarize in PR and ping infra for staging capacity. Thanks all :thumbsup:
